messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing JSON.parse errors in the JS SDK when streaming long responses. Only happens under load when the client is slow.

maria: Example raw SSE we've captured: 
``` 
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hel"}


data: lo","timestamp":16777216}


data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":", worl"}}]}
```

maria: Parser sees `data:` events and tries to parse each one — but we get truncated objects and `Unexpected end of JSON input`.

jonathan: Is the server sending proper line breaks between events? Looks like some events are single fields and some are complete objects.

maria: Server is sending full `data:` lines but the body of a logical JSON message is split across multiple `data:` events. Previously our client assumed each `data:` contained a self-contained JSON blob.

kai: That's the classic SSE chunking thing — streams can split anywhere. We shouldn't JSON.parse per `data:` line. Need to accumulate until we detect end-of-message. For NDJSON we use `\n` delim, but SSE doesn't guarantee a single-line JSON per event.

alice: For JS/node clients my recommendation: use a small stateful accumulator buffer and only attempt parse when you see a blank line between events (SSE event boundary) and the accumulated text looks like balanced braces. Or simpler: buffer until a full top-level `}` with same brace depth and not in string.

maria: Tried naive brace-counting — failed with strings containing `}`.

jonathan: Right, brace-counting needs to handle quotes and escapes. We use a tiny streaming JSON parser (clarinet or streaming-json-parser) in the SDK to be robust. That avoids brittle heuristics.

kai: Another angle — backpressure. When the consumer queue gets large the Node readable stream pumps lots of chunks into our parser which increases memory usage and makes the parser see fragments in weird boundaries. Are we applying backpressure at the writer side?

maria: Our current code does an eventlistener for `data` and `on('data', chunk => pushToQueue(chunk))` which uses an unbounded queue.

alice: Change to using the stream's `readable`/`pause()`/`resume()` semantics or `for await (const chunk of stream)` in Node — that gives you natural backpressure. Also tune `highWaterMark`. For example: `const res = await fetch(); const reader = res.body.getReader();` in the browser, call `await reader.read()` per iteration and only queue when under threshold.

jonathan: For node fetch (undici) you can `const reader = res.body[Symbol.asyncIterator]();` then `for await (const chunk of reader)` will only pull when you await.

maria: Good call. We're also seeing heartbeats from the infra like `: keepalive` (colon-prefixed) which our parser currently ignores happily, but if we use a parser that expects strict NDJSON we'll choke.

kai: Recommended pattern: treat colon-only lines as heartbeats — ignore them at the framing layer before handing textual payload to the JSON parser. That keeps parsing simpler.

alice: Also, for token refresh we sometimes abort the connection mid-stream and reconnect; that causes partial messages to be lost and misinterpreted as parse errors on the reconnect path. Consider preserving an in-flight buffer keyed by request id and resume processing after reconnect when server replays from last ack token or include a `stream_cursor` protocol so server can resume.

maria: For immediate fix I'm planning to: 1) stop JSON.parse-per-data, 2) introduce a tiny streaming parser (clarinet) fallback, 3) switch to `for await` consumption to apply backpressure, 4) ignore `: ping` lines at framing layer.

jonathan: Sounds good. One extra micro-optimization — in Node set `highWaterMark` to something like 16kb by default for streaming LLM responses; too high and you fill memory during token surges.

kai: Also measure queue length and if > N, call `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` or `await drain()` using backpressure primitives so you don't allocate huge arrays.

maria: I'll open a PR with the parser swap + test harness that injects split-chunk cases (including multibyte UTF-8 boundaries, quotes with escaped braces, and heartbeat lines).

stream-bot: deploy-bot: roll queued: devex:pr/421 landed to staging — watch for streaming regressions :eyes:

maria: Thanks — will smoke test and post results. If folks want to pair on the parser tests ping me.

jonathan: If you need a quick in-memory repro I can hack a tiny server that deliberately splits JSON mid-codepoint and emits `: ping` every 30s.

maria: Please do. That will be super helpful.

alice: Also add an optional `framing=ndjson|sse` client option so users can pick their expected server semantics; default remains SSE robust mode.

maria: Yep — will include that config and a note in changelog.

maria: TL;DR: fix is parser + proper backpressure + heartbeat ignoring. Will follow up with PR link and test results.
